checks.label: We want the coefficients of one variable to be opposites, so that we can add the equations together and eliminate that variable: at every stepper setting on every screen, opposite matching terms cancel when the rows are added and double when one is taken away, and matching terms of the same sign the other way round

Sometimes equations need to be altered, by multiplying throughout, before being able to eliminate one of the variables: each stepper multiplies every term of its row, the right side too, so the row draws the very same line, and on the scaling screens nothing cancels until a row is scaled

When eliminating a variable from a system of linear equations, 76% of students in one study misjudged the operations to be performed: the add-or-take-away screen says so, and there adding doubles the 2y to 4y while taking away leaves 0

Any point that fits both rows fits their sum: at every stepper setting and switch position on every screen, the sum row is true at the crossing, so its dotted line passes through it, standing upright when y cancels and lying flat when x cancels
The first screen adds 2x + y = 11 and 3x − y = 9: the sum row reads 5x + 0 = 20 with the 0 marked as y cancelling, and its dotted line stands upright at x = 4 through the crossing (4, 3)

Every worked line is right, by hand: 5x = 20 so x = 4 and 8 + y = 11 gives y = 3; added, 4x + 4y = 28 is 16 + 12 = 28 at (4, 3); 2y = 6 so y = 3; 5y = 15 and 2x + 9 = 17; 3x + (2x − 1) = 14 gives x = 3 and y = 5; and the worked example, 35x − 10y = 130 plus 12x + 10y = 58, gives 47x = 188 and (4, 1)

Every puzzle's answers are checked against its own two equations: the right one is what the steppers and switch really give, or the pair that fits both rows; every wrong one keeps both letters, is false at the crossing, draws a different line, matches nothing, or misses a row; and every wrong answer has a hint of its own

Before an answer a puzzle keeps back the sum row, its dotted line, the crossing ring and the working; a right answer or Why? fills the sum row in, marks the letter that cancels, and draws the dotted line upright or flat through the crossing

A wrong pick shows its slip: the wrong switch doubles the matching term, a right side added after a left side taken away shows red, half a pair stops with y still to find, a row scaled on one side only draws a different line, steppers that match nothing say so, and a wrong pair is put into both rows

Playing with a screen: a stepper at × 5 stays at × 5 and one at × 1 stays at × 1; on the scale-first screen, row 1 at × 2 with take away cancels y, leaving 5x = 20 and an upright line at x = 4, while × 3 leaves both letters and a tilted line
Every demonstration finishes arriving within its 3 to 5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends, and a puzzle's drawing after an answer or Why? finishes within 2.5 s
